content_units: You have a credible path into instructional design within   9 months   because your teaching background already maps strongly to core ID work: needs analysis, learning objectives, curriculum design, facilitation, assessment, and stakeholder communication. The main challenge is not “can you do the work,” but   translating classroom experience into corporate L&D language   and showing evidence through a small, polished portfolio.
-   eLearning Developer   only if you build stronger authoring-tool skills
-   CAD 70,000+ is realistic  , but easier with:
- Remote-only is possible, but   hybrid opens more roles faster   in Toronto.
Option 1: Learning design foundation   You already write objectives, sequence content, scaffold complexity, and assess learning   Strongest asset
Option 2: Facilitation and presentation   Public speaking and classroom delivery map well to workshops, facilitator guides, and SME sessions   High employer value
Option 3: Stakeholder communication   Teaching requires explaining clearly, managing expectations, and adapting to varied audiences   Useful for SME collaboration
Option 4: Content production basics   Google Workspace and Canva give you a base for storyboards, job aids, decks, and visual learning assets   Easy to upgrade quickly
- Move from “what should students learn?” to “what business problem is training solving?”
- Most common gap; employers often want Articulate Storyline or Rise
- LMS basics, SCORM/xAPI terminology, accessibility basics
- Hiring managers want to see samples, not just teaching experience
- More concise, performance-focused, and business-outcome oriented than school settings
- Familiarity with Kirkpatrick, ADDIE, SAM, adult learning principles, scenario-based learning
2.   Instructional design process for corporate training
Month 1   Reposition your background   Rewrite resume in L&D language; update LinkedIn headline; review 30 Toronto job posts; identify common tools/skills   Target-role resume + keyword list
Months 2-3   Build core ID capability   Learn ADDIE; adult learning; needs analysis; storyboard writing; start Articulate Rise or Storyline   1 storyboard + 1 microlearning sample
Months 4-5   Create visible portfolio   Build 2-3 polished projects; write case studies; show design choices and outcomes   Portfolio site with 3 samples
Months 6-7   Gain market credibility   Apply selectively; network with Toronto L&D professionals; attend webinars; do mock interviews   Referral pipeline + interview stories
Months 8-9   Convert to offers   Increase application volume; tailor resume per role; practice demos/interviews; target hybrid GTA roles   Offer-ready candidacy
Portfolio Projects That Make You Employable
- Build a   5–8 minute module   in Rise or Storyline
- Best for proving you understand   corporate training structure
- Create a branching scenario such as:
- Best for proving   adult-learning design   and   performance-based thinking
- Convert one of your strongest history lessons into a   corporate workshop format
- Reframe the topic to something business-relevant, such as:
- Use Canva or Google Slides to create:
- This is fast to build and useful for applications to   L&D Specialist   roles
- Pick a workplace problem like low adoption of a new process
- This helps offset your lack of direct corporate experience
Priority 1: Target adjacent roles, not only “Instructional Designer”
Apply first to roles where teaching experience is easiest to translate:
-   Onboarding / Training Coordinator   if salary path is strong
These can be easier entry points than highly technical ID jobs asking for years of Storyline and LMS admin experience.
Priority 2: Focus on sectors with stronger fit
-   Large employers with internal L&D teams
In Toronto, public and broader institutional employers may value your education background more than fast-moving startups.
- jobs asking for 2–3 years corporate ID experience but where your portfolio covers the gap
Priority 4: Customize your resume around business outcomes
Replace school-centric wording with corporate L&D language.
- “Designed outcome-based learning experiences aligned to learner needs, assessment criteria, and engagement goals”
- “Facilitated learning for large, diverse audiences and adapted delivery using assessment data and learner feedback”
Priority 5: Network in a focused, repeatable way
- connect with   5 Toronto/GTA IDs or L&D managers
- attend   1 webinar, meetup, or virtual event
- follow up with a portfolio link once ready
Priority 6: Treat LinkedIn as part of your portfolio
Your headline should signal the transition clearly:
-   High School Teacher Transitioning to Instructional Design   Learning Design, Facilitation, Curriculum Development
-   Aspiring Instructional Designer   7 Years in Education   Learning Experience Design   Toronto
- redesigning a lesson after poor results
- “Strong educator, but can they design for workplace performance?”
- clear explanation of how you solve performance problems, not just teach content
-   Entry/bridge L&D roles  : often below or around your target
-   Instructional Designer with strong portfolio  : better chance at   CAD 70,000+
-   Public sector, higher ed, healthcare, financial services  : often stronger for your target than small companies
- Apply to   mid-sized and large organizations
- Start with   Rise   if you want faster portfolio output; choose   Storyline   if more jobs you target explicitly ask for it.
- Apply by   month 4 or 5  , not only after you feel “fully ready.”
- If needed, accept a   bridge title   that leads to CAD 70,000+ within 12–18 months.
